title: Tesla's Flying Roadster Is Really a Balloon Trick

lines.text: Tesla says its new Roadster can fly,
lines.label: TESLA ROADSTER

lines.text: and this week it showed something closer to a jump.
lines.label: FLY OR JUMP?

lines.text: That jump works like a balloon you blow up and let go,
which shoots off because the air rushing out the back pushes it forward.
lines.label: PUSH

lines.text: So the Roadster carries ten small jets
lines.label: 10 JETS

lines.text: fed by six hundred litres of compressed air.
lines.label: 600 LITRES

lines.text: Then at the reveal in Texas, that push lifted it up a ramp,
lines.label: WACO, TEXAS

lines.text: spun it, and carried it over a row of Tesla cars.
lines.label: THE HOP

lines.text: The physics behind it is Newton's third law,
lines.label: NEWTON'S 3RD LAW

lines.text: which says every push comes with an equal push back.
lines.label: PUSH = PUSH BACK

lines.text: Inside, the air is squeezed into carbon-fibre tanks at very high pressure,
lines.label: HIGH PRESSURE

lines.text: and when a valve opens it blasts out of the jets,
shoving the car the opposite way, just like the balloon.
Point the jets at the ground and the car rises.
lines.label: LIFT

lines.text: But a balloon empties in seconds,
lines.label: SECONDS

lines.text: and a heavy car burns through its air just as fast,
so you get a hop, not a trip across town.
lines.label: HOP, NOT FLIGHT

lines.text: Before you believe the word flying, ask how long the air lasts.
lines.label: ASK THIS

lines.text: If that helped, follow us,
because we break down one tech story every day.
And the next time a balloon zips across your room, you'll know how Tesla's Roadster flies.
